subject: POC kickoff — ops handoff & prompt conformance session
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@nimble-retail.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Eng Team <eng-team@nimble-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff and hands-on session — routing / prompt conformance

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move to an interactive POC. We'd like to schedule a half-day working session where we can:
- Walk through our prompt inventory and examples
- Test routing behavior (customer-facing routes + fallback policy)
- Validate structured-output/JSON conformance for downstream ingestion
- Run a short loadtest (baseline 50 req/s) against representative prompts

Our preferred week is Apr 18–22. We can do either a single half-day (4 hours) or two shorter blocks. Attendees from our side will be: myself, Priya Rao (ML lead), and Marco Santos (platform).

Are you able to run this as a POC kickoff and include a short ops handoff so our infra team can mirror the routing config? Also please let us know if we need to provision anything on our side (VPN, whitelisted IPs) for the load test.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Director, AI Platforms | Nimble Retail
Samira Khan <samira@nimble-retail.com>

Attachments referenced: sample_prompts.csv (we'll send a small set before the session)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@nimble-retail.com>
Cc: Eng Team <eng-team@nimble-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and hands-on session — routing / prompt conformance

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the clear scope. We can run a focused hands-on session that covers the bullets you listed. Suggested options (PST):
- Option A: Mon Apr 18, 09:00–13:00 (single 4-hour block)
- Option B: Tue Apr 19, 09:00–11:30 & Wed Apr 20, 09:00–11:30 (two 2.5-hour blocks)

Draft agenda (can be trimmed):
1) 09:00–09:20 — Introductions & success criteria (Samira + Redwood)
2) 09:20–10:15 — Prompt inventory review (map prompts to routes)
3) 10:15–11:00 — Routing policy exercises (canary/fallback scenarios)
4) 11:00–11:30 — Structured-output schema & validation tests (JSON conformance)
5) 11:30–12:30 — Live loadtest (short runs at 25/50/100 RPS) + cost/latency profile
6) 12:30–13:00 — Ops handoff & next steps (runbook, roles, follow-ups)

Pre-reqs from your side:
- A CSV of sample prompts (attach at least 200 rows for loadtest sampling)
- IP allowlist for our load generator (if you want tests against your VPC)
- Contact for on-call infra (VPN/KMS questions)

I'll coordinate internally and propose owners for each agenda item. We can default to Option A unless you prefer the split blocks (Option B). I'll also attach a short POC runbook and a sample prompt set to this thread.

—Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: POC_Runbook_v1.xlsx, sample_prompts.csv
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: POC kickoff and hands-on session — routing / prompt conformance

Team — forwarding Samira's request and my proposed agenda. We're leaning to Option A (Mon Apr 18, 09:00–13:00). Can you each take the items below and confirm before EOD Monday?

Marissa — lead the prompt inventory review, prepare a short guardrails checklist (token limits, rejected intent handling, redaction rules). Bring the "prompt-categorization" worksheet.
Ben — set up the loadtest harness (env: dev-cluster-3), prepare three buckets for 25/50/100 RPS runs, and confirm expected GPU types and perf baselines. Include a short runbook for aborting/rolling back the test.
Stephanie — prepare a one-page security checklist: data retention, PII handling, model access controls, and audit-log locations. Also confirm if we need to run the test through the Private deployment (VPN) or if a hosted endpoint is fine for initial baseline.

I'll draft the runbook intros and own the structured-output validation tests. Please reply with quick confirmations and any blockers.

Thanks —
Alex
